hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Water ingress into unfinished buildings
hazards.definition: Rain enters through open roofs, slab edges, facade openings or unsealed penetrations, wetting interior works and services.

hazards.name: Moisture-sensitive material damage
hazards.definition: Rain wets or contaminates materials and components that must stay dry or clean (cement, rebar, insulation, drywall, joinery, M&E, asphalt, fill).

hazards.name: Interruption of concrete placement or curing
hazards.definition: Rain falling on fresh concrete or placement area alters water content/finish and can stop pours.

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Localised flooding (pluvial) of work areas and below-ground spaces
hazards.definition: Runoff or drainage overflow inundates low-lying areas, basements, lift pits, plant rooms or access routes.

hazards.name: Excavation inundation
hazards.definition: Rainwater/groundwater inflow raises water depth in an open excavation, trench, pit or shaft.

hazards.name: Ground saturation
hazards.definition: Soil pore space fills with water after sustained or repeated rain, raising pore pressure and softening surface soils.

hazards.name: Loss of soil strength
hazards.definition: Wetting reduces shear strength / stiffness of soil supporting plant, excavation faces or embankments.

hazards.name: Excavation instability (wall/face collapse)
hazards.definition: Rain or rapid water infiltration weakens excavation faces and supports, risking collapse.

hazards.name: Slope or retaining-system (ERSS) instability
hazards.definition: Increased water loading, pore pressure or erosion destabilises slopes, ERSS or retaining walls.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Reduced ground bearing capacity
hazards.definition: Softened ground cannot carry plant, cranes, falsework, scaffold bases or platforms, risking sinking or overturn.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Reduced visibility during heavy rainfall
hazards.definition: Heavy rain limits sight lines for operators, signalers, lifting and traffic.

hazards.name: Drainage and pumping capacity exceedance
hazards.definition: Inflow exceeds temporary/permanent drainage or pump capacity, producing ponding, flooding or silt carry-over.

hazards.name: Erosion and silty discharge (ECM exceedance)
hazards.definition: Rain erodes bare earth and stockpiles; silty runoff exceeds earth-control-measure capacity (regulatory/environmental consequence, not injury).

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Ground saturation
hazards.definition: Soil pore space fills with water after sustained or repeated rain, raising pore pressure and softening surface soils.

hazards.name: Loss of soil strength
hazards.definition: Wetting reduces shear strength / stiffness of soil supporting plant, excavation faces or embankments.

hazards.name: Excavation instability (wall/face collapse)
hazards.definition: Rain or rapid water infiltration weakens excavation faces and supports, risking collapse.

hazards.name: Slope or retaining-system (ERSS) instability
hazards.definition: Increased water loading, pore pressure or erosion destabilises slopes, ERSS or retaining walls.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Reduced ground bearing capacity
hazards.definition: Softened ground cannot carry plant, cranes, falsework, scaffold bases or platforms, risking sinking or overturn.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Rainwater contact with temporary electrical installations
hazards.definition: Water reaches temporary power distribution, cables, tools or plant, causing shock or short-circuit.

hazards.name: Reduced visibility during heavy rainfall
hazards.definition: Heavy rain limits sight lines for operators, signalers, lifting and traffic.

hazards.name: Rainfall-related lifting and access constraints
hazards.definition: Rain-induced loss of visibility, slippery rigging/decks and unstable ground constrain crane/hoist/MEWP operation. Wind limits are OUT OF SCOPE and not evaluated.

hazards.name: Drainage and pumping capacity exceedance
hazards.definition: Inflow exceeds temporary/permanent drainage or pump capacity, producing ponding, flooding or silt carry-over.

controls.name: Monitor forecasts and official alerts; start response before site criteria are exceeded
controls.description: Maintain weather monitoring and act proactively on alerts.

controls.name: Notification procedure to inform persons on site of impending adverse weather and actions to take
controls.description: Establish internal notification and communication channels.

controls.name: Stop work and evacuate low-ground / below-ground / excavation areas not adequately protected against flooding
controls.description: Stop work and evacuate unless the area is adequately protected against flooding.

controls.name: Protect low-lying work areas from flooding (bunds, cut-off drains, diversion)
controls.description: Physical protection of low-lying and below-ground work areas.

controls.name: Temporary and early permanent drainage, sumps and pumps sized and maintained
controls.description: Install drainage early; maintain; size for site-defined design condition.

controls.name: Standby pumps and backup power with defined discharge route
controls.description: Redundancy so pumping continues if a pump or supply fails.

controls.name: Pre-rain inspection and clearing of drains, sumps and silt traps
controls.description: Check and clear before forecast rain.
controls.source_location: SRC-07 ECM audit checklist items (cut-off drain, holding pond, treatment plant)

controls.name: Competent-person inspection of excavations, slopes and supports before work resumes after rain
controls.description: Re-assess ground stability before resumption; do not resume if unstable.

controls.name: Excavation support / ERSS designed for site water and ground conditions by a qualified engineer

controls.source_location: 'professional engineer' defined SRC-05 reg.2; operative regulation NOT verified

controls.name: Monitoring of excavation / ERSS movement and water levels against design trigger levels
controls.description: Instrument and review against design-stated trigger levels.

controls.name: Cover or protect exposed slopes, faces and stockpiles
controls.description: Cover bare surfaces and stockpiles during rain or before.

controls.name: Control surface water at excavation edges (cut-off drains, kerbs)
controls.description: Stop runoff entering the excavation.

controls.name: Haul-route and working-platform design and maintenance (hardstanding, stone, mats)
controls.description: Provide improved surfaces able to carry plant in wet conditions.
controls.source_location: s3.2.3 (wheeled vehicles confined to improved surfaces)

controls.name: Select plant suited to wet ground (e.g. tracked vs wheeled)
controls.description: Lower ground pressure plant for muddy conditions.

controls.name: Restrict or suspend earthmoving and haulage on waterlogged ground; designate routes
controls.description: Administrative restriction based on site inspection.

controls.name: Non-slip, drained and well-lit walkways and housekeeping
controls.description: Provide safe access surfaces.

controls.name: Slip-resistant footwear
controls.description: Last-line protection.
controls.source_location: Hierarchy category per SRC-01 App.C p.24

controls.name: Protect temporary electrical installations (elevated/enclosed, earth-leakage protection, competent inspection)
controls.description: Keep water away from energised parts.

controls.name: Visibility measures (lighting, spotters, speed limits, high-visibility clothing); suspend operations when visibility is inadequate

controls.name: Early envelope closure and temporary sealing/roof drainage

controls.name: Delay installation or protect permanent equipment until envelope is weathertight
controls.description: Protect M&E and finishes.

controls.description: Observe equipment in-service limits.

controls.name: Evacuation access and egress from basements/excavations (ramps, ladders, muster points)

controls.name: Identify collapse zones; evacuate or restrict persons from them
controls.description: Restrict access to potential collapse zones.

controls.name: Earth control measures per approved ECM plan by a Qualified Erosion Control Professional; maintain and audit

controls.source_location: SRC-06 ECM clauses incl. cl. 6.3 reference; SRC-07 site audit form

controls.name: Cover bare surfaces and stockpiles during rain or before
controls.description: Concrete lining, erosion blankets, turfing or equivalent.

controls.name: Drain waterlogged areas and remove accumulated water before resuming
controls.description: Recovery action.

controls.name: Re-assess ground stability; do not resume if conditions are suspected unstable or unsafe
controls.description: Recovery decision gate.

controls.name: Assess equipment safety; do not operate damaged or poor-condition equipment
controls.description: Recovery equipment check.

controls.name: Worker reporting of unsafe conditions to supervisors immediately
controls.description: Reporting culture.

controls.name: Prefabrication / off-site manufacture to reduce wet on-site exposure
controls.description: Move work into controlled environment.

controls.name: Adverse-weather training and drills
controls.description: Familiarise workers with response and evacuation.

controls.name: Identify vulnerable / at-risk workers and plan their safe evacuation
controls.description: Account for accessibility.

controls.name: Backup communications and adverse weather kit
controls.description: Walkie-talkies, loudspeakers, emergency tools.

controls.name: Contractual and schedule weather provisions (definition of inclement weather, delay allowance)
controls.description: Anticipate weather delay in contract and programme.

interventions.residual_risk_considerations: Drills do not remove the hazard

Competent-person excavation and retaining-system inspection on rain onset
Isolate affected electrical systems
Activate emergency response and rescue
Park and secure plant on stable ground; suspend earthmoving and haulage

Remove accumulated water and drain waterlogged areas

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Loss of soil strength
hazards.definition: Wetting reduces shear strength / stiffness of soil supporting plant, excavation faces or embankments.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Reduced ground bearing capacity
hazards.definition: Softened ground cannot carry plant, cranes, falsework, scaffold bases or platforms, risking sinking or overturn.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Reduced visibility during heavy rainfall
hazards.definition: Heavy rain limits sight lines for operators, signalers, lifting and traffic.

hazards.name: Erosion and silty discharge (ECM exceedance)
hazards.definition: Rain erodes bare earth and stockpiles; silty runoff exceeds earth-control-measure capacity (regulatory/environmental consequence, not injury).

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Ground saturation
hazards.definition: Soil pore space fills with water after sustained or repeated rain, raising pore pressure and softening surface soils.

hazards.name: Loss of soil strength
hazards.definition: Wetting reduces shear strength / stiffness of soil supporting plant, excavation faces or embankments.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Reduced ground bearing capacity
hazards.definition: Softened ground cannot carry plant, cranes, falsework, scaffold bases or platforms, risking sinking or overturn.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Moisture-sensitive material damage
hazards.definition: Rain wets or contaminates materials and components that must stay dry or clean (cement, rebar, insulation, drywall, joinery, M&E, asphalt, fill).

hazards.name: Erosion and silty discharge (ECM exceedance)
hazards.definition: Rain erodes bare earth and stockpiles; silty runoff exceeds earth-control-measure capacity (regulatory/environmental consequence, not injury).

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Localised flooding (pluvial) of work areas and below-ground spaces
hazards.definition: Runoff or drainage overflow inundates low-lying areas, basements, lift pits, plant rooms or access routes.

hazards.name: Loss of soil strength
hazards.definition: Wetting reduces shear strength / stiffness of soil supporting plant, excavation faces or embankments.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Reduced ground bearing capacity
hazards.definition: Softened ground cannot carry plant, cranes, falsework, scaffold bases or platforms, risking sinking or overturn.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Rainwater contact with temporary electrical installations
hazards.definition: Water reaches temporary power distribution, cables, tools or plant, causing shock or short-circuit.

hazards.name: Reduced visibility during heavy rainfall
hazards.definition: Heavy rain limits sight lines for operators, signalers, lifting and traffic.

hazards.name: Rainfall-related lifting and access constraints
hazards.definition: Rain-induced loss of visibility, slippery rigging/decks and unstable ground constrain crane/hoist/MEWP operation. Wind limits are OUT OF SCOPE and not evaluated.

hazards.name: Erosion and silty discharge (ECM exceedance)
hazards.definition: Rain erodes bare earth and stockpiles; silty runoff exceeds earth-control-measure capacity (regulatory/environmental consequence, not injury).

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Excavation inundation
hazards.definition: Rainwater/groundwater inflow raises water depth in an open excavation, trench, pit or shaft.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Moisture-sensitive material damage
hazards.definition: Rain wets or contaminates materials and components that must stay dry or clean (cement, rebar, insulation, drywall, joinery, M&E, asphalt, fill).

hazards.name: Interruption of concrete placement or curing
hazards.definition: Rain falling on fresh concrete or placement area alters water content/finish and can stop pours.

hazards.name: Waterproofing and coating application constraints
hazards.definition: Wet substrates or rain on applied membranes, sealants, plaster/render, paint or coatings prevent correct adhesion or cure.

hazards.name: Drainage and pumping capacity exceedance
hazards.definition: Inflow exceeds temporary/permanent drainage or pump capacity, producing ponding, flooding or silt carry-over.

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Excavation inundation
hazards.definition: Rainwater/groundwater inflow raises water depth in an open excavation, trench, pit or shaft.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Rainwater contact with temporary electrical installations
hazards.definition: Water reaches temporary power distribution, cables, tools or plant, causing shock or short-circuit.

hazards.name: Reduced visibility during heavy rainfall
hazards.definition: Heavy rain limits sight lines for operators, signalers, lifting and traffic.

hazards.name: Moisture-sensitive material damage
hazards.definition: Rain wets or contaminates materials and components that must stay dry or clean (cement, rebar, insulation, drywall, joinery, M&E, asphalt, fill).

hazards.name: Interruption of concrete placement or curing
hazards.definition: Rain falling on fresh concrete or placement area alters water content/finish and can stop pours.

hazards.name: Drainage and pumping capacity exceedance
hazards.definition: Inflow exceeds temporary/permanent drainage or pump capacity, producing ponding, flooding or silt carry-over.

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Localised flooding (pluvial) of work areas and below-ground spaces
hazards.definition: Runoff or drainage overflow inundates low-lying areas, basements, lift pits, plant rooms or access routes.

hazards.name: Excavation inundation
hazards.definition: Rainwater/groundwater inflow raises water depth in an open excavation, trench, pit or shaft.

hazards.name: Excavation instability (wall/face collapse)
hazards.definition: Rain or rapid water infiltration weakens excavation faces and supports, risking collapse.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Drainage and pumping capacity exceedance
hazards.definition: Inflow exceeds temporary/permanent drainage or pump capacity, producing ponding, flooding or silt carry-over.

hazards.name: Erosion and silty discharge (ECM exceedance)
hazards.definition: Rain erodes bare earth and stockpiles; silty runoff exceeds earth-control-measure capacity (regulatory/environmental consequence, not injury).

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Localised flooding (pluvial) of work areas and below-ground spaces
hazards.definition: Runoff or drainage overflow inundates low-lying areas, basements, lift pits, plant rooms or access routes.

hazards.name: Excavation inundation
hazards.definition: Rainwater/groundwater inflow raises water depth in an open excavation, trench, pit or shaft.

hazards.name: Loss of soil strength
hazards.definition: Wetting reduces shear strength / stiffness of soil supporting plant, excavation faces or embankments.

hazards.name: Excavation instability (wall/face collapse)
hazards.definition: Rain or rapid water infiltration weakens excavation faces and supports, risking collapse.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Rainwater contact with temporary electrical installations
hazards.definition: Water reaches temporary power distribution, cables, tools or plant, causing shock or short-circuit.

hazards.name: Drainage and pumping capacity exceedance
hazards.definition: Inflow exceeds temporary/permanent drainage or pump capacity, producing ponding, flooding or silt carry-over.

hazards.definition: Rain falling on fresh concrete or placement area alters water content/finish and can stop pours.

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Loss of soil strength
hazards.definition: Wetting reduces shear strength / stiffness of soil supporting plant, excavation faces or embankments.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Reduced ground bearing capacity
hazards.definition: Softened ground cannot carry plant, cranes, falsework, scaffold bases or platforms, risking sinking or overturn.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Reduced visibility during heavy rainfall
hazards.definition: Heavy rain limits sight lines for operators, signalers, lifting and traffic.

hazards.name: Moisture-sensitive material damage
hazards.definition: Rain wets or contaminates materials and components that must stay dry or clean (cement, rebar, insulation, drywall, joinery, M&E, asphalt, fill).

hazards.name: Interruption of concrete placement or curing
hazards.definition: Rain falling on fresh concrete or placement area alters water content/finish and can stop pours.

hazards.name: Erosion and silty discharge (ECM exceedance)
hazards.definition: Rain erodes bare earth and stockpiles; silty runoff exceeds earth-control-measure capacity (regulatory/environmental consequence, not injury).

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Ground saturation
hazards.definition: Soil pore space fills with water after sustained or repeated rain, raising pore pressure and softening surface soils.

hazards.name: Loss of soil strength
hazards.definition: Wetting reduces shear strength / stiffness of soil supporting plant, excavation faces or embankments.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Moisture-sensitive material damage
hazards.definition: Rain wets or contaminates materials and components that must stay dry or clean (cement, rebar, insulation, drywall, joinery, M&E, asphalt, fill).

hazards.name: Erosion and silty discharge (ECM exceedance)
hazards.definition: Rain erodes bare earth and stockpiles; silty runoff exceeds earth-control-measure capacity (regulatory/environmental consequence, not injury).

hazards.name: Surface water accumulation
hazards.definition: Rain runoff collects on work surfaces, slabs, platforms and low spots, creating standing water.

hazards.name: Slippery access surfaces
hazards.definition: Wet walkways, decks, steel, formwork, ramps or mud reduce footing and increase slips and falls.

hazards.name: Reduced ground bearing capacity
hazards.definition: Softened ground cannot carry plant, cranes, falsework, scaffold bases or platforms, risking sinking or overturn.

hazards.name: Unsafe or lost equipment/vehicle access
hazards.definition: Mud, ponding or flooding degrades haul routes and site access, forcing unsafe manoeuvres or stopping deliveries.

hazards.name: Rainwater contact with temporary electrical installations
hazards.definition: Water reaches temporary power distribution, cables, tools or plant, causing shock or short-circuit.

hazards.name: Reduced visibility during heavy rainfall
hazards.definition: Heavy rain limits sight lines for operators, signalers, lifting and traffic.

hazards.name: Erosion and silty discharge (ECM exceedance)
hazards.definition: Rain erodes bare earth and stockpiles; silty runoff exceeds earth-control-measure capacity (regulatory/environmental consequence, not injury).
